assessment.rationale: Screened all 12 allowed pressure/shelf candidate pairs from source LPN-69d7cc9079 rev 1 with the native simulator (LyoPRONTO 1.2.0), preserving the source initial shelf (−35 °C), ramps and vial/product/heat-transfer inputs. Thermal check on maximum RETURNED vial-bottom temperature vs T_pr_crit −18 °C (returned solver nodes only, no continuous-maximum guarantee). Shelf +10 °C failed the thermal check at all pressures (max returned bottom −17.07 °C at 0.05 Torr, −15.82 °C at 0.1 Torr, −13.84 °C at 0.2 Torr, all above −18 °C). 0.2 Torr/−25 °C did not reach complete drying within the 60 h horizon (88.25% dried at 60 h) so it is not a complete-drying recipe. The other eight candidates completed at 100% dried and satisfy both constraints. Fastest complete-drying feasible recipe: 0.2 Torr / −5 °C shelf, complete at 17.786 h. Thermal margin: −18.0 − (−18.6979) = 0.6979 °C below the critical on returned vial-bottom nodes. Capacity margin derived from native outputs: peak returned flux 0.6312301662673401 kg/h/m² × whole-batch product area 0.125012 m² (398 vials × 3.14 cm²/vial) = 0.078911 kg/h whole-batch peak, vs equipment line −0.182 + 11.7 × 0.2 Torr = 2.158 kg/h → margin 2.079 kg/h. Native simulated values, not measured outcomes; authored simulator-world synthetic case, not experimental validation or an approval.

**Selected recipe: 0.2 Torr / −5 °C shelf — fastest complete-drying candidate that satisfies both constraints.**

- **Predicted complete drying: 17.79 h** (dried 100% at 17.786154 h; horizon 60 h, reached).
- **Thermal constraint:** max returned vial-bottom temperature −18.698 °C ≤ T_pr_crit (−18.0 °C). Margin: **−0.698 °C** (0.698 °C below the limit).
- **Equipment line constraint:** capacity = −0.182 + 11.7 × 0.2 = **2.158 kg/h** whole-batch. Peak batch sublimation = 0.956475 kg/h/m² × 0.125072 m² (398 vials × 3.14 cm²) = **0.1196 kg/h** (derived). Capacity margin: **2.038 kg/h**.

Why not faster: all three 10 °C-shelf runs finish sooner (10.97–13.02 h) but their max returned bottom temperatures (−17.07, −15.82, −13.84 °C) exceed the −18 °C critical. The 0.2 Torr/−25 °C run did not complete (88.25% dried at the 60 h horizon) and is excluded. Next-fastest feasible: 0.1 Torr/−5 °C at 18.85 h (max bottom −20.58 °C) and 0.05 Torr/−5 °C at 19.67 h. These are native solver results on returned nodes with no continuous-maximum guarantee, not measured outcomes or approvals.

output.content:
**Selected recipe: 0.2 Torr chamber pressure with a −5 °C shelf — the fastest complete-drying candidate that meets both constraints.** Predicted primary-drying completion: **17.79 h** (17.786 h from the native solver). The assessment is saved as a draft (not a manufacturing approval) with all 12 native simulation results attached.

**Constraint margins (at the selected pair):**
- **Thermal:** maximum returned vial-bottom temperature **−18.70 °C** vs the critical **−18.0 °C** → margin **0.70 °C** below the critical.
- **Equipment line:** peak returned flux **0.631 kg/h/m²** × whole-batch product area **0.125 m²** (398 vials × 3.14 cm²) = **0.079 kg/h** whole-batch peak — a derived conversion, since the native model returns per-square-metre flux — vs the equipment line **−0.182 + 11.7 × 0.2 Torr = 2.158 kg/h** → margin **2.08 kg/h**.

**Screen evidence (all 12 allowed pairs, native LyoPRONTO 1.2.0 runs on the source case):** the +10 °C shelf failed the thermal check at every pressure (max returned bottom −17.07 °C at 0.05 Torr, −15.82 °C at 0.1 Torr, −13.84 °C at 0.2 Torr — all above −18 °C); 0.2 Torr/−25 °C did not reach complete drying within the 60 h horizon (88.25% dried at 60 h), so it is not a complete-drying recipe; the remaining eight candidates completed at 100% dried within both constraints, and 0.2 Torr/−5 °C was the fastest.

**What I could not check:** both constraints were evaluated on the solver's returned nodes only — the source itself states there is no continuous-maximum guarantee, so a brief excursion above −18 °C between nodes cannot be ruled out. The equipment-line comparison uses the source's own a+b·P coefficients and my flux-to-batch conversion, not a measured condenser or ice-collection rate. This is a synthetic, authored simulator-world case: nothing here is a measured outcome, experimental validation, or equipment operation, and I did not use internal process models. The saved assessment remains in draft, awaiting review.
